A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. The original proofs and numerical analyses can be matched across the appendix reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original computational experiments using PEP/SDP optimization, including contraction-rate grids, numerical discrepancies, multistep convergence and step-size comparisons in Section 3 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains those computational results and adds comparisons with previous EF21 guarantees, including an original experiment optimizing the previous Lyapunov family's weighting in Appendix D.5.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3, the EF/EF21 optimal step-size rules, and the PEP, bisection, log-det and symbolic-regression procedure are retained. The stochastic-compressor extension broadens the guarantees without changing the algorithms.

E1.justification: Numerical evaluation remains within single-agent, smooth strongly convex optimization with deterministic compressors. V2 explicitly confirms this in Section 3.1; its stochastic extension is theoretical, and the new sparse-training citation does not introduce an evaluated task.

E2.justification: V2 adds quantitative comparisons against Richtárik et al.'s published EF21 rate in Appendix B and an optimally reweighted version of their Lyapunov family in Appendix D.5. These comparators were discussed but not evaluated in the corresponding v1 analyses.

E3.justification: New comparisons introduce the log-contraction ratio as a complexity metric and optimize the relative weighting within the previous EF21 Lyapunov family. Retained experiments preserve the 200-point grids, bisection precision, solver procedure and cycle-detection threshold.

E4.justification: Appendix D.5 adds a targeted control testing whether the previous EF21 Lyapunov family remains inferior after optimizing its relative weighting. Existing multistep tightness, Lyapunov-class tightness and step-size analyses are retained from v1 Appendix C.

E5.justification: Neither version introduces repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. V2's checklist explains that the experiments are deterministic. The retained absolute-error tables measure numerical agreement rather than statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: V2 adds rate and complexity comparisons against the published EF21 bound in Figures 2–3, CGD/error-feedback complexity ratios in Figure 5, and the reweighted-Lyapunov comparison in Figure 12. Tables 1–4 retain their values after matching reordered columns, and the original EF/EF21 equivalence and CGD-superiority findings remain.

T1.justification: Assumption 1 expands from deterministic contractivity to stochastic contractivity in expectation, supported by the new Appendix C.3 argument. Appendix B adds analytical comparisons with CGD and the previous EF21 rate. V2 also corrects the relative-gradient-error bound in Section 2.1 and the EF21 Lyapunov identity in Equation (13).

C1.justification: V2 withdraws the claim that this is the first application of performance estimation to compressed federated-learning algorithms and explicitly extends its tight guarantees to stochastic compressors. The principal claims of optimal EF/EF21 tuning, equal complexities and CGD superiority in the single-agent setting remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds a connection between single-agent error feedback and sparse-update training, and distinguishes deterministic numerical validation from stochastic guarantees. Appendix E explains the scope of CAS/PEP checks and identifies full formal verification as future work. The multi-agent limitation is retained.

D1.justification: V2 adds statement-specific links to CAS scripts and PEP notebooks, including stochastic-compressor certificates, and explains their verification roles. V1 already disclosed the repository, software and hardware. The new checklist inconsistently describes code release as forthcoming despite retaining the public-repository disclosure; external availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 adds Lin et al. on dynamic pruning, Gannot on inexact gradients, and De Klerk et al. on exact line search. It strengthens positioning against previous EF21 analysis and removes the first-application novelty claim while retaining the broader literature review.

P1.justification: Most existing exposition and proof prose is retained. V2 adds a front-page certificate explanation, supplementary comparison and certificate sections, and a checklist, alongside localized wording edits. The original proof and numerical appendices become C and D rather than being replaced.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands the visual presentation with new comparison Figures 2, 3, 5 and 12, prominent colored certificate boxes, and theorem badges. V1 Figure 2 is redrawn and relocated as v2 Figure 4; retained tables and plots also receive ordering, labeling and placement adjustments.

improvement.justification: V2 improves mathematical precision, explicitly supports stochastic compressors, and strengthens comparison with previous EF21 analysis through analytical arguments and the reweighted-Lyapunov control. Certificate-specific links improve traceability. The central results were already present in v1, while the added checklist introduces stale scope and code-access statements, making the net quality gain useful but limited.
